patch_resolves_note: The official patch.diff did not apply in the ARVO workspace, so the fixed-side evidence comes from the authoritative 25910-fix image. On that fixed build the original 32-byte witness still emits `parse_result_gate`, but `parseResult` is non-OK and the compatibility-call and sink assertion events do not execute.

root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `parseResult != AVIF_RESULT_OK` after `avifParse(decoder)` has handled the duplicate malformed top-level `ftyp`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: After `avifParse(decoder)` returns from the duplicate zero-payload top-level `ftyp`, `avifDecoderParse()` must observe a non-OK `parseResult` and stop before the compatibility check runs.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original converts the failed second `avifParseFileTypeBox()` into numeric `AVIF_RESULT_OK`, so `avifDecoderParse()` falls through into `avifFileTypeIsCompatible()` with stale `decoder->data->ftyp` aliases still live. The fixed image returns a non-OK parse result for the same witness, so the compatibility check is never reached.

nodes.state: At the compatibility-call site, `decoder->data->ftypData.data` is already NULL because the duplicate zero-length `ftyp` replacement freed and cleared the owned `ftypData` buffer before the stale alias is reused downstream.

The first compatibility-loop iteration passes `compatibleBrand` to `memcmp()`, and in the vulnerable run that pointer is the preserved first-`ftyp` alias into the heap region already freed by the duplicate zero-payload replacement.

edges.relation: The same `parseResult` value observed at the error gate remains `AVIF_RESULT_OK` at the compatibility-call site, so control falls through into `avifFileTypeIsCompatible()` instead of returning on the malformed duplicate `ftyp`.

The `compatibleBrands` pointer stored during the first `ftyp` parse is still the pointer observed at the later compatibility-call site, even though the owned `ftypData` buffer has already been cleared.
The preserved `decoder->data->ftyp.compatibleBrands` pointer is dereferenced as `compatibleBrand` in the first compatibility-loop iteration, carrying the stale alias directly to the `memcmp()` sink.
